name: create_trigger
description: Create a natural-language trigger for the current user. A trigger has an **if** condition (`trigger_nl_condition` — when to fire) and a list of **actions** (what to deliver and where when it fires). Each action carries its own message; a fire delivers every action. Only call this after the user has explicitly asked to create a trigger — do not create speculatively. To deliver somewhere specific (e.g. a Slack channel), call `get_destination_configs` first and use one of the returned ids; omit `destination_config_id` to record to the event log.

scope_path.description: Wiki-relative path of the file or directory to watch. Use a `.md` path (e.g. `auth/passwords.md`) to watch one doc, or a directory path (e.g. `auth`) to watch every doc beneath it. Use `/` (or an empty string) to watch the whole wiki.

trigger_nl_condition.description: **If condition.** Plain-language description of when the trigger should fire (e.g. "when the auth flow's session-timeout policy changes"). Evaluated by an LLM against the diff, so be specific about what kind of change matters.

actions.description: **What to deliver, and where.** One entry per delivery. Most triggers have exactly one.

message.description: The notification body delivered when the trigger fires (e.g. "Auth: session timeout policy changed — please review").

destination_config_id.description: A destination config id from `get_destination_configs` (the user's own delivery targets). Omit to record the fire in the event log only.
